name: CC2520RHDR
title: CC2520: 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.15.4 / ZigBee RF transceiver, QFN28 5 x 5 mm
summary: A 2.4 GHz transceiver chip for IEEE 802.15.4 and ZigBee: 250 kbps DSSS O-QPSK from 2394 MHz to 2507 MHz, -98 dBm sensitivity and up to +5 dBm output, run from 1.8 V to 3.8 V over -40 °C to 125 °C. It handles framing, CRC, frame filtering, automatic ACK, CCA, RSSI and AES-128 security in hardware, with 768 bytes of RAM, a 4-wire SPI up to 8 MHz and six configurable GPIOs. It needs a 32 MHz crystal, a 56 kΩ bias resistor and an external balun and antenna.
key_figures: 33.6 mA at +5 dBm, 25.8 mA at 0 dBm

circuits.title: Typical application with transmission-line balun, single-ended antenna
circuits.description: The transceiver with its few outside parts. All supply pins, DVDD and AVDD_GUARD included, share one 1.8 V to 3.8 V rail. DCOUPL carries only its decoupling capacitor C271. RBIAS returns to ground through the 56 kΩ 1 % resistor R231. A 32 MHz crystal sits across XOSC32M_Q1 and XOSC32M_Q2 with load capacitors C121 and C131. The differential RF pins feed a balun of three transmission lines (TL1 to TL3) and capacitors C171 to C174, C191 and C192 that presents the right termination to the chip when the antenna port is 50 Ω. The SPI, RESETn, VREG_EN and the six GPIOs go to the MCU. Each supply pin takes its own decoupling capacitor, fed in a star; their values are in the reference design bill of materials.
notes: The balun line lengths and the values of C172, C173, C174 and C192 depend on the board layout.
The NC pins 15, 18 and 21 may float.

circuits.title: Interconnection with MSP430F2618
circuits.description: The digital wiring used on the development kit: the MSP430F2618 drives VREG_EN and RESETn from port pins, talks over its USCI_B1 SPI (SCLK, SI, SO, CSn) and takes all six GPIOs on timer and port pins.

operation.text: A 2.4 GHz direct-conversion transceiver for IEEE 802.15.4 (2006) and ZigBee: DSSS O-QPSK with half-sine shaping, 250 kbps, 2 Mchip/s, 2394 MHz to 2507 MHz. Each byte splits into two 4-bit symbols, low symbol first; each symbol maps to one of 16 32-chip sequences.

An MCU drives the chip over SPI and GPIO. An instruction decoder runs instructions; an exception controller turns events into flags that can fire instructions or drive GPIO interrupts. 768 bytes of RAM hold the 128-byte TX and RX FIFOs and working memory. A data processing unit with an AES-128 core runs the memory and security instructions. The radio FSM sequences calibration, CCA, frame length counting, FCS checking and automatic ACKs.
An on-chip regulator feeds the 1.8 V digital core through DCOUPL; its current limit acts above about 32 mA. DCOUPL must not supply other devices.

LPM2: VREG_EN low, regulator off, no clocks, nothing retained, 30 nA typical. LPM1: regulator on, no clocks, state kept, 175 µA typical. Active mode: regulator and crystal oscillator running, 1.6 mA. After LPM2 a reset is needed (RESETn low, or SRES) and the register-update values must be written again. Resetting before entering LPM2 is advised.

Raise VREG_EN with RESETn low and keep RESETn low at least 0.1 ms while the regulator settles. Releasing RESETn starts the crystal oscillator, which takes about 0.2 ms with the reference crystal. With CSn low, SO goes high once the oscillator is stable, with no SCLK edge needed. GPIOs take their reset configuration while RESETn is low.
After the regulator has settled, take CSn low and send SRES, then SXOSCON, because SRES does not start the oscillator. Until SRES the chip state is undefined, and it could even be transmitting.

The four SPI lines are required. RESETn is best driven by the MCU; tied to VDD, resets use SRES plus SXOSCON. VREG_EN from the MCU allows LPM2; tied to VDD the regulator stays on. GPIOs are optional; more of them means less reconfiguration over SPI. GPIO0 can clock the MCU: it gives 1 MHz, 50 % duty, after reset.

Mode: data set up on falling SCLK, sampled on rising, MSB first, up to 8 MHz with no minimum and SCLK may pause. CSn low for more than two 32 MHz periods before the first rising SCLK edge and after the last falling one, and high for at least two periods. The status byte comes out during the first byte of each instruction. Register access needs the crystal oscillator running. Variable-length instructions end when CSn rises; raising CSn inside a byte gives SPI_ERROR.

Six GPIOs, each set by GPIOCTRLn: bit 7 picks input or output and the low 7 bits pick the signal or, as input, one of 16 command strobes fired on the edge chosen in GPIOPOLARITY. GPIOCTRL holds the pull-ups, extra drive and the analog function of GPIO0 and GPIO1. Pull-ups are off after reset and in LPM2. To turn an output into a strobe input without a false trigger: write 0x7E (constant 0), drive 0 from the MCU, then write the input code. Inputs have Schmitt triggers.
In LPM2, GPIO5 is an input and must be tied to ground or VDD; other GPIOs grounded or high impedance; SO must not float. Floating inputs raise current unpredictably.

A glitch-free divider gives a 50 % duty clock of 1 MHz to 16 MHz on a GPIO, 1 MHz on GPIO0 after reset, so one crystal can serve chip and MCU; it needs active mode. To wake: MCU on its RC oscillator, bring the CC2520 to active mode, switch the MCU to the 1 MHz clock, then change frequency. To sleep: MCU to RC oscillator first, then LPM2.

STXON starts a frame; STXONCCA starts it only if CCA is high. Preamble begins 192 µs after the strobe. SRXON, SRFOFF or a new STXON abort it. The 128-byte TX FIFO holds one frame and may be filled during transmission. With FRMCTRL0.AUTOCRC set the chip appends the 2-byte FCS, which the length field still counts. After the frame the modulator ramps down for 2 µs, which stretches SFD and the return to idle by 2 µs. SFD and TX_FRM_DONE exceptions mark start and end.

SRXON and SRFOFF switch RX hard; RXENABLE bits switch it softly without aborting a frame in progress. RX is ready 192 µs after enabling, and by default SFD search pauses 192 µs after each received frame. The RX FIFO can hold several frames. Hardware does frame filtering, source address matching, FCS checking and automatic ACKs. FIFO and FIFOP pins signal data; on overflow FIFO = 0 and FIFOP = 1, cleared with SFLUSHRX.

RSSI is a signed 1 dB/LSB value averaged over 8 symbols (128 µs), valid once RX has run 8 symbol periods (RSSI_VALID). It can be read or appended to frames. CCA compares RSSI with a programmable threshold (CCACTRL0/1); a continuously updated and a strobe-sampled version are both in FSMSTAT1, and CCA follows RSSI_VALID by 4 cycles of 32 MHz. Neither RSSI nor CCA is valid in low-current RX mode.

Three register changes cut wait-for-sync current to 18.8 mA at the cost of sensitivity (-90 dBm) and of interferer rejection at strong signals. RSSI and CCA are then invalid, so STXONCCA cannot be used. Valid only from -40 °C to 85 °C.
Output power drops markedly over -40 °C to 125 °C. Changing TXPOWER with temperature, and above 70 °C using the F7125deg setting (TXCTRL 0x94, FSCTRL 0x7B), keeps it near 1 dBm to 4 dBm.

Set GPIOCTRL0 and GPIOCTRL1 to 0x80 (inputs), set GPIOCTRL.GPIO_ACTRL, and write 0x01 to ATEST. GPIO1 then outputs ground and GPIO0 a voltage proportional to temperature, about 0.8 V at 25 °C and 2.5 mV/°C, read with the MCU ADC.

The reference must be 32 MHz, parallel resonant, between XOSC32M_Q1 and XOSC32M_Q2 with two load capacitors. The oscillator is amplitude regulated: high current to start, then just enough to sustain, so crystal ESR must stay within 60 Ω. A single-ended clock may drive XOSC32M_Q1 instead of a crystal. Keep the two crystal traces apart.

RF_P and RF_N form a high-impedance differential port; a single-ended antenna needs a balun of discrete L and C parts, or of transmission lines with capacitors as on the two-layer reference design. The balun is layout sensitive; its line lengths and capacitors must be fitted to the board.

Copy the reference design layout. Feed the supplies in a star with a decoupling capacitor close to each power pin. Keep digital input traces away from noisy signals. The reference design offers an SMA connector, selected by a 0 Ω resistor, or a planar inverted-F PCB antenna; characterization used the SMA.

The chip must be in RX, settled (RSSI valid), to make random bits. A GPIO can output single bits from the I or Q channel, or their XOR, at 8 MHz; the RANDOM instruction reads bytes over SPI built from the I channel LSB. Over 20 million bytes the mean was 127.65, a small DC bias.

Frames sent or received are copied out on two GPIOs as sniff_clk (250 kHz) and sniff_data, MSB of each byte first, once enabled in MDMTEST1; an SPI slave can take the stream. In TX the two auto-CRC bytes go out as 0x8080 instead. The sfd signal on a third GPIO gives time stamps.
AES-128 instructions cover ECB, CTR, CBC-MAC and CCM/CCM* encryption and authentication on data in RAM, each run at high or low priority, with keys and nonces held in RAM.
The exposed pad (pin 29) must be soldered to the board for heat and mechanical strength.
